reader.requirement: At 1985 an ADD, COMPUTE, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY or SUBTRACT whose numeric operands (DISPLAY with any SIGN form, COMPUTATIONAL, BINARY, PACKED-DECIMAL; scaled by V or P; signed or unsigned; numeric literals and ZERO) and resultants (numeric or numeric-edited) have differing descriptions must compute the exact decimal result, supplying every conversion and decimal-point alignment itself; the witness covers DISPLAY/BINARY/PACKED/SIGN LEADING SEPARATE operands and edited receivers but not P-scaled items, COMPUTATIONAL, SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE, figurative ZERO, the 18-digit edge or table/ODO operands.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal (active from 2002): at 1985 an unphrased statement takes the two-phase shape that catches every raise and continues; the conversion/alignment renders inside it are the same code
data.Edition.MaxDigits (18 at 1985, 31 later) and ReceivingItems85 composite membership (Edition.Year < 2002); a GR2 refusal on the same statements, not the conversion itself
the ARITHMETIC IS mode; 1985 has no ARITHMETIC clause so the native lane is taken, the same lane the latest edition takes by default

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|DialectBehaviors|EditionContext|CobolVersion over ArithmeticEmitter.cs, NumericRenderer.cs, ReceiverBracketEmitter.cs, EmitCore.cs, SendingValueTemp.cs, ExpressionBinder.cs; the only arithmetic-store hits are EmitArith:719 and UnsignedSubsidiary:264 (DIVIDE REMAINDER only)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the conversion and alignment render is edition-independent; only the size-error disposition and the 18-digit composite cap differ
